problem: RNN-based image-goal navigation policies compress history into one state vector, do poorly on long-horizon navigation, and are trained by online RL that needs hundreds of millions of episodes and heavy compute.
motivation: Image-goal navigation needs scene understanding, memory and long-horizon planning without maps. Transformers model long sequences and multiple modalities well but are hard to train with online RL, so the paper trains a Transformer offline with goal-conditioned behavior cloning on expert trajectories.
key_idea: Train a decoder-only Decision-Transformer-style model, with the goal-image token first in the sequence and interleaved observation and action tokens, by goal-conditioned behavior cloning on successful trajectories from a pretrained OVRL-v2 expert.
insight: A small Transformer (27M trainable parameters) trained offline on one GPU beats other behavior-cloned baselines on Gibson-curved (6.78 vs 1.70 SR) while remaining far below the RL expert (45.60 SR). This shows that BC alone leaves a large gap to online RL. Offline action accuracy is higher on hard episodes than on easy ones, which the author attributes to the model learning the expert's generic exploration behavior.
method: Goal-conditioned BC data: successful OVRL-v2 (expert) trajectories on the Gibson train split (9000 episodes per scene) form the expert dataset; 96K curved trajectories are sampled for training
Image encoder: frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with registers; patch tokens from the last 4 layers plus the CLS token are concatenated and passed through a 2-layer MLP to d=384

Action embedding and tokens: discrete actions go through a learnable lookup table, are shifted right, and are interleaved with image embeddings as [E_I1,E_a1,...]; the goal embedding is prepended to the sequence
Position embedding: a learnable embedding shared by the image and action tokens of the same timestep
Decoder: 12-layer pre-LN causal Transformer, 8 heads, FFN dim 1024, context T=8 timesteps; no returns-to-go, conditioning is on the goal token only

Actor head and inference: an MLP outputs action logits, trained with cross-entropy; at inference top-k (k=2) sampling replaces greedy decoding to avoid repeated actions and getting stuck, with a FIFO buffer of the last 8 observations and actions

setting.backbone: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 w/ registers (frozen) + 12-layer decoder-only Transformer (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 96K successful OVRL-v2 expert trajectories from the Gibson curved train split (9000 episodes x 72 scenes, ZER split); 20 epochs, subsequences of length 8
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 128x128, 90° FOV; no depth, no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: discrete: STOP, MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT 30°, TURN_RIGHT 30°
setting.privileged: none at test time; expert trajectories from OVRL-v2 (trained with RL) are used for training and only successful episodes are kept

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson-curved: random sample of 300 of 1000 episodes (Hahn et al. split); episode length capped at 100 (easy) and 350 (medium/hard)
numbers.extra: trained by behavior cloning on 96K OVRL-v2 expert trajectories; reduced step limits; 128x128 RGB
numbers.evidence: Table autoreg_results, Gibson-curved, Ours Overall 6.78 / 6.37 (Easy 16.00/15.08, Medium 3.67/3.49, Hard 0.67/0.54)

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson-straight: random sample of 300 of 1000 episodes; episode length capped at 100 (easy) and 350 (medium/hard)
numbers.extra: trained only on curved episodes; BC from OVRL-v2 expert; 128x128 RGB
numbers.evidence: Table autoreg_results, Gibson-straight, Ours Overall 15.06 / 14.04 (Easy 28.33/26.13, Medium 11.33/10.53, Hard 4.00/3.65)

numbers_note: The Gibson test split names are not official ones; the 'test' label is assigned to the Hahn et al. curved/straight test episodes. Offline action accuracies (75.45-80.49%) are in Table 2 but are not navigation metrics.
results: On Gibson-curved the model reaches 6.78 SR / 6.37 SPL against 1.70 / 1.30 for BC with GRU (the strongest BC baseline), and on Gibson-straight 15.06 / 14.04, which is below BC-GRU (19.50 / 18.70) but above BC with spatial memory (12.50 / 12.10). It is far below the OVRL-v2 RL expert (45.60 SR curved, 44.90 SR straight).
limitations: Success rates are low and far below the RL expert. The evaluation uses only a 300-episode subset with shortened step limits, and the expert-success filter biases the data.

The model cannot see low obstacles and cannot recover from collisions, because it has no depth, pose or reward and its training data are biased against collisions. It also fails on blank-wall goal images and narrow hallways.
Offline action accuracy is only 75-80%, and no ablations are reported for encoder, context length or top-k sampling.
compares_to: Behavior Cloning w/ Spatial Memory (No RL, Long Way Home)
